author: paullizer
body:
## Latest Features (v0.191.0)

1. **Azure API Management (APIM) Support**  
   - **New APIM Toggles**: In the Admin Settings, you can now enable or disable APIM usage separately for GPT, embeddings, and image generation.  
   - **APIM Endpoints & Subscription Keys**: For each AI service (GPT, Embeddings, Image Generation), you can specify an APIM endpoint, version, deployment, and subscription key—allowing a unified API gateway approach (e.g., rate limiting, authentication) without changing your core service code.  
   - **Seamless Switching**: A single checkbox (`Enable APIM`) within each tab (GPT, Embeddings, Image Generation) instantly switches the app between native Azure endpoints and APIM-protected endpoints, with no redeployment required.

2. **Enhanced Admin Settings UI**  
   - **Advanced Fields**: Collapsible “Show Advanced” sections for GPT, Embeddings, and Image Generation let you configure API versions or other fine-tuning details only when needed.  
   - **Test Connectivity**: Each service tab (GPT, Embeddings, Image Gen) now has a dedicated “Test Connection” button, providing immediate feedback on whether your settings and credentials are valid.  
   - **Improved UX for Keys**: Updated show/hide password toggles for all key fields (including APIM subscription keys), making it easier to confirm you’ve entered credentials correctly.

3. **External APIs Refreshed**  
   - **New Form Layout**: The “External APIs” tab has been refined for chunking or embedding endpoints outside of Azure OpenAI, aligning the UI design with the rest of the Admin Settings.  
   - **Connection Testing**: A dedicated “Test Connection” button has been added to verify external chunking or embedding services before saving changes.

4. **Miscellaneous Improvements**  
   - **UI Polishing**: Minor styling updates and improved tooltips in Admin Settings to guide first-time users.  
   - **Performance Tweaks**: Reduced initial load time for the Admin Settings page when large model lists are returned from the OpenAI endpoints.  
   - **Logging & Error Handling**: More descriptive error messages and client-side alerts for failed fetches (e.g., if the user tries to fetch GPT models but hasn’t set the endpoint properly).

With these additions in **v0.191.0**, the Simple Chat Application offers more flexible deployment options (via APIM), easier debugging through one-click connectivity tests, and a cleaner Admin Settings experience for managing AI services.

author: fthiery
body:
The current LG Soundbar integration does not report when the device is offline. The original integration relies on the https://github.com/google/python-temescal dependency, which is dead.

Note that this PR requires the following fork: https://github.com/fthiery/python-temescal -- especially this commit: https://github.com/fthiery/python-temescal/commit/e80ad7157737a651792634c2543a844f72f1982c

I am unsure how to switch HA to use my version (either publish the package under a different name, or ask the original author to let me update pypi), but before i do that, please let me know if my approach seems acceptable.

## Breaking change

This introduces a heartbeat mecanism, which sends an arbitrarily selected information retrieval command to determine whether the TCP connection is alive and well; in other terms, this will increase traffic (one command every 10 seconds), and the LED display will stay active (but power consumption stays identical).

The core problem was that nothing made it easy to detect when the device was gone; i implemented a keepalive mecanism in the dependency, which allows for offline detection.

body:
This PR tweaks the signal overview plots a little to make them more compact, to better handle situations where many signals are present at the same locus and start to stack up very high.

Also changes back to colouring all signals the same colour (red) rather than trying to colour by taxon - this was potentially confusing and I thought it might be just simpler to keep all signals the same.

Also to help with consistent plotting of signals across different pages, some common functions are factored out into a site-utils.py script which can be run from other notebooks.

## Pull Request Description

### Title: 
feature/PWA-Initial

### Description:
This pull request introduces initial support for Progressive Web App (PWA) features in the To-Do application. The following changes have been made:

- **PWA Support**: Installed and configured PWA support in `vite.config.js` to enable offline capabilities and enhance user experience.
- **Manifest and Service Worker**: Added a PWA manifest file along with an icon (`icon.png`) to define the app's appearance and behavior when installed on devices. Edited the service worker to improve caching strategies.
- **Local Storage Management**: Implemented task management functionality with localStorage support, allowing users to persist their tasks even after refreshing the page.
- **PWA Install Prompt**: Integrated an install prompt for the PWA, encouraging users to add the app to their home screen for easier access.
- **Task Priority Feature**: Added the ability to select and update task priorities, enhancing task management capabilities.
- **Styling Enhancements**: Improved the overall styling of the application with a reset and layout adjustments for a better user interface.
- **Bug Fixes**: Addressed issue #2 related to the screenshot for the PWA and manifest.

These enhancements aim to provide a more robust and user-friendly experience for the To-Do application, leveraging PWA capabilities for better performance and accessibility. 

### Related Issues:
- Fixes #2: Screenshot for the PWA and manifest fix

body:
Add functions to Nightsoul module to allow setting up NS with an optional cb for when NS status ends. This CB will only be called if NS expires via the timer, not if NS is manually expired, and is intended to clean up the character state on Nightsoul expiry. As an alternative, an OnNightsoulExpiry event could be used, or an array of cb functions could be allowed.

Kinich refactored to make use of this functionality.

GCSL users can get remaining NS duration through .<character>.status.nightsoul-blessing.

For now, it's assumed that all NS timers will be hitlag extended. If that is not the case, code can be further refactored to accept a hitlag bool, to be passed through to the char.AddStatus method call.

I manually tested a few Kinich configs and got matching results, but I have not run a full DB compare.
If desired, I can split this PR into two; one for NS changes and one for Kinich changes.

author: yukinamochizuki
body:
## Type of changes
Feature

## Purpose
Introduced a new user type "Service Account", enabling internal services (e.g. recommended system) to have permanent verification credentials to access `/api/internal` endpoints.

To streamline setup, the `application.service.account.default.token` property has been added, allowing the backend to automatically create a Service Account named `default` with the role `ROLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_READ` upon startup. If not set, it won't be created.

When a new Service Account is created, a UUID will be automatically generated as a token and returned only once. If the token is lost, the Service Account must be deleted and recreated.

## Additional Information
### Endpoints
- `GET /api/internal/service-account/me`
- `GET /api/internal/service-accounts`
- `POST /api/internal/service-accounts`
- `DELETE /api/internal/service-account/{{uuid}}`

This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **7.6.1** to **7.6.11**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#pep-649-deferred-evaluation-of-annotations


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``
  statements changed how they traced.  This affected whether people saw the
  fix for `issue 1880`_.

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases
  can cause `bizarre behavior <pytest-cov-666_>`_.

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to
  asserts.  If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

.. _pytest-cov-666: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666


.. _changes_7-6-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra
  "didn't," as described in `issue 1873`_.  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1873: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1873
.. _issue 1876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1876


.. _changes_7-6-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: a final wildcard match/case clause assigning to a name (``case _ as
  value``) was incorrectly marked as a missing branch.  This is now fixed,
  closing `issue 1860`_.

- Fewer things are considered branches now. Lambdas, comprehensions, and
  generator expressions are no longer marked as missing branches if they don't
  complete execution.  Closes `issue 1852`_.

- Fix: the HTML report didn't properly show multi-line f-strings that end with
  a backslash continuation.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 1836`_, thanks
  to `LiuYinCarl and Marco Ricci <pull 1838_>`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report now has correct line numbers (fixing `issue 1846`_) and
  better branch descriptions for BRDA records (fixing `issue 1850`_).  There
  are other changes to lcov also, including a new configuration option
  :ref:`line_checksums <config_lcov_line_checksums>` to control whether line
  checksums are included in the lcov report.  The default is false. To keep
  checksums set it to true.  All this work is thanks to Zack Weinberg
  (`pull 1849`_ and `pull 1851`_).

- Fixed the docs for multi-line regex exclusions, closing `issue 1863`_.
   ```

body:
Part of https://discord.com/channels/181078474394566657/1334957536519913513
and https://discord.com/channels/181078474394566657/1329023562979213353

As mentioned in the design doc of the mega retier AOI, one of the main issues of cryogenic freezer is getting large quantities of cryotheum, unlike the hot counterpart of this, the pyrotheum

This removes tiny and small dusts from EEC and changes the output to be:
- 25% blizz rod
- 50% blizz dust
- 2% cryotheum

Makes the blizz rod maceration recipe to be like blaze rod, with 3 full dust output and 1 dust at 50%

Replace the chemical bath recipe of blizz dust to use 100L liquid nitrogen and 4 blaze powder, resulting in 4 blizz dusts

Makes the freezer recipe for blizz rod 4 times faster

Makes snow block and snow ball output 4 times more snow dust, and also removing small dust output


This would help making cryotheum be similar to pyrotheum

author: vncero
body:
# Description

Please include a summary of the changes and the related issue. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

`MathUtils::deadband`, which is used for driver input, is redundant as WPILib's [`MathUtil::applyDeadband`](https://github.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/blob/b60b2b64bd14f842c3a6ff4ee83f4c6be918d8e9/wpimath/src/main/java/edu/wpi/first/math/MathUtil.java#L102) is roughly equivalent in function. The only difference is that `MathUtil::applyDeadband` scales the range from deadband to maximum (1.0) from 0.0 to 1.0 while `MathUtils::deadband` leaves said range untouched. `MathUtils::epsilonEquals` is removed both for not being used anywhere and for being redundant due to WPILib's [`MathUtil::isNear`](https://github.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/blob/b60b2b64bd14f842c3a6ff4ee83f4c6be918d8e9/wpimath/src/main/java/edu/wpi/first/math/MathUtil.java#L178), which is identical except for parameter order and even adds a guard against negative epsilon/tolerance values. `MathUtils::squareKeepSign` does not duplicate the functionality of an existing WPILib function, but it is not used anywhere and should be removed if left unused in future commits.

## Type of change

<!-- Guidelines: https://docs.spacestation14.io/en/getting-started/pr-guideline -->

## About the PR
<!-- What did you change? -->
<!-- If this is a code change, summarize at high level how your new code works. This makes it easier to review. -->

Fixes an issue where droppable items weren't being considered in equality checks for duplicated modules.  This led to some cases where modules were considered duplicates (e.g. fire extinguisher and jetpack) because their set of fixed items is empty.

## Why / Balance
<!-- Discuss how this would affect game balance or explain why it was changed. Link any relevant discussions or issues. -->

Impromptu bug report from Discord.

## How to test
<!-- Describe the way it can be tested -->

1. Spawn a borg, inhabit it, pick the generic chassis, exit the borg.
2. Spawn two fire extinguisher modules and two jetpack modules.
3. Unlock and screwdriver the borg.
4. Try to insert both fire extinguisher modules.  The first should work, the second should fail (it's duplicated).
5. Try to insert both jetpack modules.  The first should work (the bug has been fixed), the second should fail (it's duplicated).
6. Repeat with the GPS module (only fixed items).
7. Inhabit the borg, drop your fire extinguisher, swap back to your other character, try to insert the fire extinguisher module, it should still fail (duplicated).

This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **6.0.2** to **7.6.11**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#pep-649-deferred-evaluation-of-annotations


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``
  statements changed how they traced.  This affected whether people saw the
  fix for `issue 1880`_.

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases
  can cause `bizarre behavior <pytest-cov-666_>`_.

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to
  asserts.  If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

.. _pytest-cov-666: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666


.. _changes_7-6-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra
  "didn't," as described in `issue 1873`_.  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1873: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1873
.. _issue 1876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1876


.. _changes_7-6-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: a final wildcard match/case clause assigning to a name (``case _ as
  value``) was incorrectly marked as a missing branch.  This is now fixed,
  closing `issue 1860`_.

- Fewer things are considered branches now. Lambdas, comprehensions, and
  generator expressions are no longer marked as missing branches if they don't
  complete execution.  Closes `issue 1852`_.

- Fix: the HTML report didn't properly show multi-line f-strings that end with
  a backslash continuation.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 1836`_, thanks
  to `LiuYinCarl and Marco Ricci <pull 1838_>`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report now has correct line numbers (fixing `issue 1846`_) and
  better branch descriptions for BRDA records (fixing `issue 1850`_).  There
  are other changes to lcov also, including a new configuration option
  :ref:`line_checksums <config_lcov_line_checksums>` to control whether line
  checksums are included in the lcov report.  The default is false. To keep
  checksums set it to true.  All this work is thanks to Zack Weinberg
  (`pull 1849`_ and `pull 1851`_).

- Fixed the docs for multi-line regex exclusions, closing `issue 1863`_.

- Fixed a potential crash in the C tracer, closing `issue 1835`_, thanks to
  `Jan Kühle <pull 1843_>`_.

.. _issue 1835: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1835
.. _issue 1836: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1836
.. _pull 1838: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1838
.. _pull 1843: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1843
.. _issue 1846: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1846
.. _pull 1849: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1849
.. _issue 1850: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1850
.. _pull 1851: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1851
.. _issue 1852: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1852
.. _issue 1860: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1860
.. _issue 1863: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1863


.. _changes_7-6-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: coverage used to fail when measuring code using :func:`runpy.run_path
  <python:runpy.run_path>` with a :class:`Path <python:pathlib.Path>` argument.
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Ask Hjorth Larsen <pull 1819_>`_.

- Fix: backslashes preceding a multi-line backslashed string could confuse the
  HTML report.  This is now fixed, thanks to `LiuYinCarl <pull 1828_>`_.

- Now we publish wheels for Python 3.13, both regular and free-threaded.

.. _pull 1819: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1819
.. _pull 1828: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1828


.. _changes_7-6-0:
   ```

body:
## Overview
This PR introduces Cursor Tools integration to enhance our development workflow for the HCCC FastAPI SSO project. Cursor Tools will provide AI-assisted development capabilities, helping us maintain our production-first approach while accelerating development.

## Key Features

### 1. Context-Aware Development
- **Repository Context**: Using `cursor-tools repo` for intelligent codebase understanding
- **Web Research**: Integrated `cursor-tools web` for best practices and solutions research
- **Documentation Generation**: Automated documentation capabilities with `cursor-tools doc`

### 2. Production-First Development Support
- Semantic search across codebase to maintain consistency
- Automated documentation generation following our established standards
- Browser automation tools for testing frontend integration

### 3. Implementation Assistance for Remaining Roadmap Items
- Database Setup (SQLAlchemy & PostgreSQL)
  - Intelligent code generation following our established patterns
  - Automated testing suggestions based on codebase context
  - Best practices research integration

- User Model & Authentication
  - Pattern-aware code generation for models and schemas
  - Security best practices integration
  - Automated test case generation

- API Endpoints
  - Consistent endpoint implementation across versions
  - Automated OpenAPI documentation
  - Integration test suggestions

## Technical Details
- Global installation of Cursor Tools for consistent team usage
- Configuration stored in `~/.cursor-tools/.env`
- Local research documentation stored in `local-research/`
- Integration with existing project rules in `.cursor/rules/`

## Benefits
1. **Consistency**: Ensures all generated code follows our established patterns
2. **Efficiency**: Reduces development time while maintaining quality
3. **Documentation**: Automated, consistent documentation generation
4. **Research**: Integrated best practices research for implementation decisions
5. **Testing**: Intelligent test case generation and validation

## Next Steps
1. Complete Docker infrastructure setup for development/testing environments
2. Implement database layer with Cursor Tools assistance
3. Progress through remaining roadmap items with AI-assisted development

## Testing
- All Cursor Tools commands have been verified
- Documentation generation tested
- Repository context queries validated

## Notes
- Team members should run `npx cursor-tools@latest` to access the tools
- API keys are managed securely in the global configuration
- Local research findings are committed for team reference

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.1** to **7.6.11**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#pep-649-deferred-evaluation-of-annotations


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``
  statements changed how they traced.  This affected whether people saw the
  fix for `issue 1880`_.

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases
  can cause `bizarre behavior <pytest-cov-666_>`_.

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to
  asserts.  If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

.. _pytest-cov-666: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666


.. _changes_7-6-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra
  "didn't," as described in `issue 1873`_.  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1873: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1873
.. _issue 1876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1876


.. _changes_7-6-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: a final wildcard match/case clause assigning to a name (``case _ as
  value``) was incorrectly marked as a missing branch.  This is now fixed,
  closing `issue 1860`_.

- Fewer things are considered branches now. Lambdas, comprehensions, and
  generator expressions are no longer marked as missing branches if they don't
  complete execution.  Closes `issue 1852`_.

- Fix: the HTML report didn't properly show multi-line f-strings that end with
  a backslash continuation.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 1836`_, thanks
  to `LiuYinCarl and Marco Ricci <pull 1838_>`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report now has correct line numbers (fixing `issue 1846`_) and
  better branch descriptions for BRDA records (fixing `issue 1850`_).  There
  are other changes to lcov also, including a new configuration option
  :ref:`line_checksums <config_lcov_line_checksums>` to control whether line
  checksums are included in the lcov report.  The default is false. To keep
  checksums set it to true.  All this work is thanks to Zack Weinberg
  (`pull 1849`_ and `pull 1851`_).

- Fixed the docs for multi-line regex exclusions, closing `issue 1863`_.

- Fixed a potential crash in the C tracer, closing `issue 1835`_, thanks to
  `Jan Kühle <pull 1843_>`_.

.. _issue 1835: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1835
.. _issue 1836: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1836
.. _pull 1838: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1838
.. _pull 1843: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1843
.. _issue 1846: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1846
.. _pull 1849: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1849
.. _issue 1850: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1850
.. _pull 1851: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1851
.. _issue 1852: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1852
.. _issue 1860: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1860
.. _issue 1863: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1863


.. _changes_7-6-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: coverage used to fail when measuring code using :func:`runpy.run_path
  <python:runpy.run_path>` with a :class:`Path <python:pathlib.Path>` argument.
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Ask Hjorth Larsen <pull 1819_>`_.

- Fix: backslashes preceding a multi-line backslashed string could confuse the
  HTML report.  This is now fixed, thanks to `LiuYinCarl <pull 1828_>`_.

- Now we publish wheels for Python 3.13, both regular and free-threaded.

.. _pull 1819: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1819
.. _pull 1828: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1828


.. _changes_7-6-0:
   ```

This enhancement adds a new "Base Kiosk" mode, accessible from Desktop Activity pages.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e80dbd6b-4dc4-45d6-b38f-1334bc782d46)

Accessing this mode allows users to manage their roster entries from a shared computer; e.g. at the command post. Similarly, it will allow users to add/update other responders to the roster.

On the Kiosk page, start by selecting which Organization to associate new roster entries with:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cca1bd6e-ff09-4691-a135-7c1040a21185)

Next, a search box appears which queries the MemberProvider for the selected Organization, entering a few characters will start a query:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a5ddf8f-433a-4829-a1a7-e4c7729816df)

The status updater on this page updates the status of the currently selected member:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3da67c7f-158e-4b3a-9f62-9b283bb9589a)

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.3.1** to **7.6.11**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#pep-649-deferred-evaluation-of-annotations


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``
  statements changed how they traced.  This affected whether people saw the
  fix for `issue 1880`_.

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases
  can cause `bizarre behavior <pytest-cov-666_>`_.

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to
  asserts.  If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

.. _pytest-cov-666: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666


.. _changes_7-6-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra
  "didn't," as described in `issue 1873`_.  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1873: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1873
.. _issue 1876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1876


.. _changes_7-6-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: a final wildcard match/case clause assigning to a name (``case _ as
  value``) was incorrectly marked as a missing branch.  This is now fixed,
  closing `issue 1860`_.

- Fewer things are considered branches now. Lambdas, comprehensions, and
  generator expressions are no longer marked as missing branches if they don't
  complete execution.  Closes `issue 1852`_.

- Fix: the HTML report didn't properly show multi-line f-strings that end with
  a backslash continuation.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 1836`_, thanks
  to `LiuYinCarl and Marco Ricci <pull 1838_>`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report now has correct line numbers (fixing `issue 1846`_) and
  better branch descriptions for BRDA records (fixing `issue 1850`_).  There
  are other changes to lcov also, including a new configuration option
  :ref:`line_checksums <config_lcov_line_checksums>` to control whether line
  checksums are included in the lcov report.  The default is false. To keep
  checksums set it to true.  All this work is thanks to Zack Weinberg
  (`pull 1849`_ and `pull 1851`_).

- Fixed the docs for multi-line regex exclusions, closing `issue 1863`_.

- Fixed a potential crash in the C tracer, closing `issue 1835`_, thanks to
  `Jan Kühle <pull 1843_>`_.

.. _issue 1835: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1835
.. _issue 1836: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1836
.. _pull 1838: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1838
.. _pull 1843: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1843
.. _issue 1846: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1846
.. _pull 1849: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1849
.. _issue 1850: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1850
.. _pull 1851: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1851
.. _issue 1852: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1852
.. _issue 1860: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1860
.. _issue 1863: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1863


.. _changes_7-6-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: coverage used to fail when measuring code using :func:`runpy.run_path
  <python:runpy.run_path>` with a :class:`Path <python:pathlib.Path>` argument.
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Ask Hjorth Larsen <pull 1819_>`_.

- Fix: backslashes preceding a multi-line backslashed string could confuse the
  HTML report.  This is now fixed, thanks to `LiuYinCarl <pull 1828_>`_.

- Now we publish wheels for Python 3.13, both regular and free-threaded.

.. _pull 1819: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1819
.. _pull 1828: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1828


.. _changes_7-6-0:
   ```

author: jamilbk
body:
Whether we execute a task on the main thread or a background thread doesn't affect whether the thread is "hung" as reported by Sentry.

Instead, our options for fixing these are:

- Try to use an async version of the underlying API (the [async version](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace/open(_:configuration:completionhandler:)) of `open` for example)
- If there is none, and the call could potentially block (most likely to do disk IO contention), at least schedule this on a new thread using `Task.detached` but with `.background` priority so that it will avoid blocking any other execution.

The main takeaway here is that unfortunately, under some conditions, Sentry will _always_ report an "App Hanging" alert since it's constantly monitoring all threads for paused execution longer than 2000ms.

We'll probably end up letting some of these slide (pausing a background or worker thread isn't necessarily a UX issue), but pausing the UI thread is.

Luckily, we're able to use async APIs for most things. The remaining things (like working with log files over IPC) we use a `Task.detached` for.

author: radarhere
body:
Borrowing an idea from #5201. Similar to #8734

As shown at https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/typeobj.html#examples, this uses member names to initialize `PyTypeObject`s, rather than being verbose and going through every member in sequence.

Also, I've removed specifying `tp_flags` as `Py_TPFLAGS_DEFAULT`, and so instead using the actual default from https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/typeobj.html#c.PyTypeObject.tp_flags, `Py_TPFLAGS_DEFAULT | Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE`. 

https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/typeobj.html#c.Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE
> **Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE**
> This bit is set when the type can be used as the base type of another type. If this bit is clear, the type cannot be subtyped (similar to a “final” class in Java).

I don't think we really need to specify that they can't be subtyped.

- [x] sessionStorage에 웹소켓 연결 state 저장
- [x] storageController 분리하여 언제든 localstorage로 변경할 수 있도록 추상화
- [x] cookie 관련 로직 제거 (httpOnly 설정되어 있어서 건드릴 수 없다. 그러나 localhost에서 쿠키가 제대로 유지되지 않는다.)
- [x] 새로고침 시에, 웹소켓 기존 연결 끊고 새로 연결되도록 설정
- [x] 닉네임 없으면 웹소켓 연결 아예 시도하지 않도록 변경
- [x] 투표 유효 시간 지나면 스토리지에서 닉네임과 uuid 제거하도록 설정

### ✨ 개발 내용

<!-- 개발에 대한 내용을 적어주세요 -->

```
AS-IS: 새로고침 시에 웹소켓 재연결하도록 설정 (결국 서로 다른 웹소켓 세션이 열리는 구조)
TO-BE: SharedWorker 사용하여 하나의 웹소켓 세션만 존재하도록 설정

(고민점 + 궁금한점)
1. 웹소켓 세션이 여러 개 존재할 경우에는 서로 다른 세션끼리 데이터 공유가 안 되는 구조인가?
- voteUuid, nickname을 헤더에 담아 웹소켓 세션을 연결한다.
- SESSIONID를 쿠키에 담아보낸다.
- 메시지 publish 할 때, voteUuid 경로에 설정한다.
- 그럼에도, 세션이 다르면 동일한 정보를 보여줄 수 없는가?

2. 만약 동일한 정보를 보여줄 수 있다면, 하나의 웹소켓 세션을 고집해야 하는 이유는 서버의 부하를 줄이기 위해서인가?
- 현재 구조는 새로고침 시에는 무조건 새 웹소켓 세션이 열린다.
- 이를 브라우저의 백그라운드 서비스에서 SharedWorker를 사용하면 각 유저 별로 여러 개의 탭을 열어놔도 하나의 세션만 열리게 처리한다.
- 이 구조가 필요한 것인가?

추가) 유저 별로 각기 다른 세션이 열릴텐데, 어차피 유저가 10명이라면 10개의 웹소켓 세션이 열릴 것이다. 새로고침을 방지해야하는 이유가 하나의 세션만 열기 위함이라면 애초에 불가능한 구조가 아닌가.
```

### 🚨 TroubleShooting

<!-- TroubleShotting이 있었다면 이야기 해주세요! -->
- 만약, 새로고침 시에 웹소켓 세션을 재생성하지 않기 위해 sessionStorage 또는 localStorage에서 연결 상태를 저장하여 기존 연결 상태를 참고하여 새로운 세션을 재생성하지 않도록 처리한다면 ?
-> 현재 clientRef는 새로고침 시에 어차피 null로 초기화된다. 따라서, null인 client에 메시지를 전송하고 구독하는 꼴이 되기 때문에 통신이 제대로 이루어지지 않는다.
- 만약, clientRef가 비어있으면 재연결해서 client를 null이 아니게 만들어준다면 ?
-> 새로운 웹소켓 세션이 열린다.

author: srhirsh
body:
**Added Functionality**
- Created figure_scripts directory to contain the tools described in the subsequent bullet points
- Created combined_workers.py, a class for generating and configuring complete analyses pipelines (processing, post-processing, and assessments)
- Created confidence_maps.py, a command line tool for generating MaskRCNN inference confidence maps for images (one for each instance and one combined)
- Created trials.py, a command line tool for running trials (repeated processing of images) to study the effect of randomized line placements on MLI, examine how varying the number of lines affects MLI, and determine whether AlveolEye is deterministic 
- Created utils.py, a handful of functions for use in combined_workers.py, confidence_maps.py, and trials.py as well as an add_range_column function for potential use by researchers seeking to describe their AlveolEye results

**Bug Fixes**
- Reprogrammed ASVD to account for the blocking label
- Added a check for division by zero in ASVD
- Modified ASVD unit tests to correspond to the new ASVD program

**Big Improvements**
- Changed how weights loading works to remove redundant logic, standardize how the code uses paths, ensure weights only download into one folder regardless of where init_trained_model is called
- Changed how import weights and import image works; file dialog now opens to correct directories reliably

**Small Improvements**
- Cleaned ASVD code
- Fixed the stated labels associated with each class in README.md
- Removed the Usage.md (it contains nothing beyond README.md)
- Renamed the "data" folder that stores the example images to "example_images" to be more precise
- Renamed _rules to _rules_engine (it contained no actual rules, just code that facilitates the creation and evaluation of rules)
- Moved the toggle function from _rules to _gui_creator (toggle performs no functionality inherently rules-related but does manipulate the GUI)
- Changed “greyscale” spelling to “grayscale”
- Renamed “clean” function to “filter_small_components” in postprocessing.py
- Made the actual MLI line a different color from its padding
- Refactored default weights folder from "data" to "default weights"
- Changed remove small particles/holes defaults for better default post-processing
- Added an export function that generates a unique file name by appending a number to the end if the current file name is used in the desired export location

body:
Directly using getAuth, as mentioned in the docs creates a reference error with the message: `ReferenceError: getAuth is not defined`. However, importing and destructuring it alongside clerkMiddleware and requireAuth as `import { clerkMiddleware, requireAuth, getAuth } from "@clerk/express";` resolves the issue

### 🔎 Previews:

- [Clerk Express Quickstart - Protect Your Routes Using requireAuth](https://clerk.com/docs/quickstarts/express#protect-your-routes-using-require-auth)

### What does this solve?

- Directly using `getAuth` as documented results in a `ReferenceError: getAuth is not defined`.  
- This occurs because `getAuth` is not automatically available in the scope unless explicitly imported.  
- By importing `getAuth` alongside `clerkMiddleware` and `requireAuth` as:  
  ```js
  import { clerkMiddleware, requireAuth, getAuth } from "@clerk/express";
  ```
- the issue is resolved, ensuring that `getAuth` is correctly recognized.

### What changed?

- Updated the import statement to explicitly include `getAuth`.
- Ensured that `getAuth` is properly available in the module scope to prevent reference errors.

body:
To get ready for the new payment feature, here are new fields/ tables added to the DB
```
    users {
	    stripeAccountId: String
    }
    projects {
	    transaction: ObjectId
    }
   transactions {
	    _id: ObjectId
	    project: ObjectId
	    client: ObjectId
	    professional: ObjectId
	    paymentIntentId: String
	    totalAmount: Number
	    platformFee: Number
	    status: String
	    createdAt: Date
    }
 ```

**In the codebase, I:** 
1. Added backend schemas & models & interfaces & dtos
2. Added frontend models 
3. Add functions to backend controllers
4. Connect backend controllers to front end services. Provided some simple APIs for future use

**Services currently supporting:**
1. Update the user's stripeAccountId in database
2. get a transaction from database by its ID
3. get a transaction from database by its projectID


**You can test the badkend APIs with these CURL requests (paste into Postman)**

1. Get a transaction by its ID
```
curl --location --request GET 'http://localhost:3333/api/transactions/67995e5c3c4c6632b4a38d8f' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

2. Get a transaction by the project ID it's associated with
```
curl --location --request GET 'http://localhost:3333/api/transactions/project/61a80872ab6a3b0df117fadf' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

3. Set stripeAccountId to an user

```
curl --location --request PATCH 'http://localhost:3333/api/users/stripe-account/67995e5c3c4c6632b4a38d8f' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
    "stripeAccountId": "newAccountId"
}'
```

I have tested the services briefly, you can still call the services in `ngOnInit` block of any component and log the results to see it working.

author: dayaelee
body: ## :sparkles: Week{33} {이다예} 문제풀이 - [X] 문제 1. 정수 삼각형 > ### 풀이: > > 정수 삼각형의 맨 밑단부터 한줄 씩 위로 올라가며 갱신하는 방식으로 누적합으로 구했습니다. > x-1번째 줄에 인덱스 0칸의 경우, x줄의 인덱스 0칸과 1칸을 합했을 때 나올 수 있는 값 중 큰 값으로 갱신했습니다. > > ### 느낀점: > > 문제를 고정된 시각이 아닌 다양한 각도로 바라보고 풀이 방법을 고민해보는 것이 향후 다른 문제를 풀때도 큰 도움이 될 것 같습니다. - [X] 문제 2. {사전} > ### 풀이: > > 점화식을 스스로 세울 수 없어서 인터넷에 있는 다른 코드를 참고하여 작성후 완벽 이해하는 과정을 거쳤습니다. 주석을 통해 상황에 맞는 세세한 풀이를 작성해두었습니다. > > 1. dp 배열의 자료형을 double로 사용한 이유 > > - 조합의 개수는 매우 빠르게 증가하며, 최대 10^29(100경) 이상이 될 수 있음 > - int(약 21억)와 long(약 9경)보다 더 큰 값을 저장하기 위해 double 사용함 > - double은 실수형이지만, 정확한 값이 아닌 "10억보다 크냐?"만 판단하면 되므로 문제없음 > - BigInteger도 사용 가능하지만, 객체 기반이므로 연산 속도가 느려 부적합함 > > 2. StringBuilder를 전역으로 선언한 이유 > > - 하나의 객체를 재사용하여 성능 최적화를 하기 위함 > - String을 사용할 경우, 문자열 수정 시 새 객체가 생성되어 성능 저하가 발생함 > - StringBuilder는 기존 객체를 수정하는 방식이므로 메모리 절약이 가능함 > > 3. check(a, z) 함수 (조합 계산) > > - (a, z)로 만들 수 있는 문자열 개수를 계산하는 함수임 > - dp 배열을 활용하여 중복 연산을 방지함 > - 점화식: > - check(a, z) = check(a-1, z) + check(a, z-1) > - (맨 앞에 a가 오는 경우 + 맨 앞에 z가 오는 경우) > - 최댓값을 10억+1로 제한하여 불필요한을 계산 방지함 > > 4. makeString(a, z, k) 함수 (k번째 문자열 생성) > > - a와 z의 개수를 기반으로 k번째 문자열을 생성함 > - 남은 a 또는 z가 0개이면 남은 문자를 모두 추가하고 종료함 > - check(a-1, z)를 이용해 맨 앞 문자를 결정함 > - k가 check(a-1, z)보다 크면 맨 앞은 z이고, k를 줄여 makeString(a, z-1, k-check) 호출함 > - k가 check(a-1, z)보다 작으면 맨 앞은 a이고, makeString(a-1, z, k) 호출함 > > ### 느낀점: > > 아직 자바 문법이 익숙하지 않은데, 이번 문제를 통해서 많이 배울 수 있었습니다. 조합을 활용하는 문자열 문제 유형에 대한 풀이 방법을 이해할 수 있었습니다. > - [x] 문제3. 세 용액 > ### 풀이: > > 이 문제도 저에게는 어려운 난이도로 느껴져서(스스로 주어진 용액을 정렬하는것 까지 하였음) 다른분의 코드를 참고하여 작성후 완벽 이해하는 과정을 거쳤습니다. > > 1. 정렬 > 2. 주어진 용액을 전부 순회 > 3. 2번에서 순회하는 값 외에 나머지 2개의 값에 대해서는 투포인터로 조회하며 특성값이 0에 가까운지 체크함 > > ### 느낀점: > > 투포인터에 대한 개념이 부족해서 따로 정리하며 문제를 이해할 수 있어서 학습에 많은 도움이 되었습니다.

author: senglert7
body:
In the past (pre-2025), tournaments could invite teams they wanted, even if they where not yet ranked on the VRS. This allowed new teams with semi popular players (not good enough for Wildcard invites, but well known in the Tier 2/3 scene) to enter the ranking by playing 10 games or more. For those teams open qualifiers are now the only possiblity to enter the ranking. Winning one open qualifier will most likely not be enough to reach 10 games even with the following closed qualifier. Even winning two could not be enough. And the number of open qualifiers are limited. 

Thus in 2025, the filter for when a team needs to be in the ranking should be reduced from 10 to a lower number (e.g. 5). Additionally it would make sense to also base this filter on merit and not just on played games. My suggestion is thus, to change the filter to number of games won instead. My suggested value would be 3 games won.

author: k900
body:
3ad12b6 added username validation, but only validated the username provided as part of the join event. When joining with an external token, the username needs to be loaded from the token instead.

This broke in two ways:
- in the default UI, the username would be passed in as "" with token auth, which failed validation even if the token was valid
- you could pass in a valid username in the join event, and then pass in an invalid one in the token, and that would be accepted and used, presumably allowing for the same shenanigans 3ad12b6 sought to prevent

Move username validation to the end, where we know what the right username is.

author: synrg
body:
This PR modernizes the taxon menu, bringing it up to the same standards and look-and-feel as our model `,life` and `,taxon list` commands. All menu, source, and formatter concerns are split off and moved down to **dronefly-discord** and **dronefly-core** as needed. When complete, it will finally resolve #141 .

The commands affected are `,taxon` and all of its subcommands and variants (e.g. `,img` is included as a taxon command), as well as `,tab` and all of its subcommands, as both sets of commands support *social buttons*.

### Concepts

- *Social buttons* are buttons that any registered user can use to update the menu. For example, the 👤 button is a *social button* to add or remove the user's own stats for the current display.

### Tasks

- [x] Convert reaction menu to component-based menu.
- [x] Eliminate round-trip to read/write the message each time a user presses a *social button*.
- [x] Use taxon count list source to handle user and place stats tables.
- [x] Use taxon count formatters for user and place entries.
- [x] Replace predicate-based user and place query with modal dialogs to handle adding arbitrary user or place (i.e. user 👥 and place 🌍 *social buttons*) privately.
- [x] Support every kind of Dronefly query count in `taxon` displays (i.e. `from`, `by`, `by id`, `not by`) 
- [x] Make menu, formatter, and source classes for use in `,tab` command
- [x] Also support all Dronefly query counts in `tab` displays (same as `taxon` but the `per` count controlled by buttons differs)
- [ ] Make interactions cache persist across cog reloads.
- [ ] Remove buttons and expire associated interaction cache when the menu messages are no longer in the Discord cache (avoids exceeding DIscord's rate limit on editing old uncached messages).

This PR introduces **end-to-end (E2E) test cases** to validate the core functionalities of the **Multi-Tenant Management System**. The test cases cover creating a new tenant, searching for an existing tenant, and deleting a tenant, ensuring a seamless workflow for tenant management.

body:
Fixes: https://github.com/inwx/terraform-provider-inwx/issues/37

- Add UpdateContext to nameserver resource
- Remove ForceNew from most resource attributes
- Implement createOrUpdateNameserver function to handle both create and update
- Add import validation with environment variable support for nameservers and SOA mail
- Implement FQDN and email validation helpers
- Improve error handling and resource state management

`terraform import` / `tofu import` usage:

API nameserver.info doesn't return `nameservers` and `soa_mail`, which are required to import a nameserver resource without triggering a force replacement. So, we need to read them from environment variables for a successful import. I don't see another reasonable way to inject this additional information and avoid resource replacement.

Example:
```
INWX_NAMESERVERS="ns1.example.com,ns2.example.com,ns3.example.com"
INWX_SOA_MAIL="admin@example.com"
tofu import inwx_nameserver.tld example.com:12345
```

This PR also contains a minor improvement in `inwx/internal/resource/resource_domain_contact.go` to satisfy go lint 
- refactor: improve code formatting and type handling in domain contact resource

author: dbalcomb
body:
This adds a new `reproduce` method to the `Selector` trait.

The `Recombinator` trait allows multiple parent individuals to be recombined into multiple output individuals. In the case of the various crossover recombinators, genes are swapped between the two parents and then both modified parents are returned. However, more often than not it is only one of the output individuals that is actually wanted. The `Take` operator adapter exists to support this but that would require the use of the turbofish syntax which not all users may be familiar with.

This change adds a new `reproduce` method to the `Selector` trait that is simply an alias to `.recombine(r).take::<1>()`.

body:
This pull request includes significant updates to the testing setup for both the backend and web components. The changes introduce new testing configurations, mock setups, and additional test cases to ensure better coverage and reliability.

### Backend Testing Enhancements:

* [`backend/__tests__/config/setup.js`](diffhunk://#diff-8cea68f0c9206c16d7eb7f3c9c0a6493eb097b2e1b5f1fbdff1de732de1f85fcR1-R31): Added mock implementations for MongoDB and Redis, and configured Jest to clear all mocks after each test.
* [`backend/__tests__/unit/hello.test.js`](diffhunk://#diff-3dd240992cd875054b2693a991201f6e5e4082409290a6c4e8a65cd8d0656a01R1-R11): Added a new test suite for a simple "Hello World" function to validate basic functionality.
* [`backend/jest.config.js`](diffhunk://#diff-f7d70e1bacea95e9c2008e5cbd7698c48ca63a1f4e7d4eb4d22d0b2db50f6aa6R1-R20): Configured Jest with a Node environment, verbose output, coverage collection, and specified test file patterns and setup files.
* [`backend/package.json`](diffhunk://#diff-495707834ca4b862f9acdfbac70d279023d2c059da13db59594e61ed3354fed5L10-R12): Updated test scripts to include `test:watch` and `test:coverage` commands.

### Web Testing Enhancements:

* [`web/package.json`](diffhunk://#diff-b861012a5dd72b8a9f3281b7cf09f5a779c98569d040b1bbc1db50f1b15e7cceL11-R14): Updated test scripts to use Vitest and added new commands for test coverage and UI. Also, added new testing dependencies such as `@testing-library/react` and `vitest`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b861012a5dd72b8a9f3281b7cf09f5a779c98569d040b1bbc1db50f1b15e7cceL11-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b861012a5dd72b8a9f3281b7cf09f5a779c98569d040b1bbc1db50f1b15e7cceR24-R40)
* [`web/src/App.test.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-dd354d6f0407e3424cb6ef6bdfa929c692b2e29667974a8de4980e89d71cc7d5R1-R8): Added a test case to verify that the Vite + React heading is rendered correctly.
* [`web/src/setupTests.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-87b0c4a098f0caa5f49d4fc4c10b1a1d6fc346ca4c65fb7378cbe5fa24e3475eR1): Imported `@testing-library/jest-dom` to extend Jest matchers for DOM node assertions.
* [`web/vitest.config.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-c3fc010b682e68f2ed0b7b1485b8aa513443a66d500903b8dff1d65908d02aaeR1-R10): Configured Vitest with globals, jsdom environment, setup files, and test file inclusion patterns.

body:
# Python API Vercel Configuration

This PR sets up our Python FastAPI backend for serverless deployment on Vercel alongside our Next.js frontend.

## Changes
- ✅ Add vercel.json configuration
- ✅ Create Vercel-specific entry point
- ✅ Configure CORS for production domains
- ✅ Update requirements.txt for serverless
- ✅ Add deployment documentation

## Testing
1. Local Development:
   ```bash
   cd apps/python-api
   docker-compose up python-api
   ```

2. Verify endpoints:
   - Health check: http://localhost:8000/health
   - API docs: http://localhost:8000/docs

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.6.11**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#pep-649-deferred-evaluation-of-annotations


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``
  statements changed how they traced.  This affected whether people saw the
  fix for `issue 1880`_.

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases
  can cause `bizarre behavior <pytest-cov-666_>`_.

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to
  asserts.  If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

.. _pytest-cov-666: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666


.. _changes_7-6-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra
  "didn't," as described in `issue 1873`_.  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1873: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1873
.. _issue 1876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1876


.. _changes_7-6-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: a final wildcard match/case clause assigning to a name (``case _ as
  value``) was incorrectly marked as a missing branch.  This is now fixed,
  closing `issue 1860`_.

- Fewer things are considered branches now. Lambdas, comprehensions, and
  generator expressions are no longer marked as missing branches if they don't
  complete execution.  Closes `issue 1852`_.

- Fix: the HTML report didn't properly show multi-line f-strings that end with
  a backslash continuation.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 1836`_, thanks
  to `LiuYinCarl and Marco Ricci <pull 1838_>`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report now has correct line numbers (fixing `issue 1846`_) and
  better branch descriptions for BRDA records (fixing `issue 1850`_).  There
  are other changes to lcov also, including a new configuration option
  :ref:`line_checksums <config_lcov_line_checksums>` to control whether line
  checksums are included in the lcov report.  The default is false. To keep
  checksums set it to true.  All this work is thanks to Zack Weinberg
  (`pull 1849`_ and `pull 1851`_).

- Fixed the docs for multi-line regex exclusions, closing `issue 1863`_.

- Fixed a potential crash in the C tracer, closing `issue 1835`_, thanks to
  `Jan Kühle <pull 1843_>`_.

.. _issue 1835: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1835
.. _issue 1836: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1836
.. _pull 1838: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1838

.. _issue 1852: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1852
.. _issue 1860: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1860
.. _issue 1863: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1863


.. _changes_7-6-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: coverage used to fail when measuring code using :func:`runpy.run_path
  <python:runpy.run_path>` with a :class:`Path <python:pathlib.Path>` argument.
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Ask Hjorth Larsen <pull 1819_>`_.

- Fix: backslashes preceding a multi-line backslashed string could confuse the
   ```

# What's changed?

- New unit tests
- Optimized CI/CD workflow(s)
- Websocket connections
- Dockerfile changes
- A bunch of new `npm run` commands
- Adjusted weird container percentage calculation I did (seriously what did i do therre?!)
- A graph generation "service" (Needs a rewrite)
- High Availability
- And more!

# Note

This took a bit longer then expected but hey atleast the Frontend gets some love as well right now (See this issue: [#56](https://github.com/Its4Nik/DockStat/issues/56))

## Summary by Sourcery

Remove Swagger annotations from routes and update documentation.

New Features:
- Add WebSocket endpoints for streaming container data and server logs.
- Introduce stack management routes for creating, starting, stopping, and retrieving stack configurations and environment variables.
- Add graph generation functionality with routes for retrieving graph data in JSON and HTML formats, as well as a PNG image of the graph.

Enhancements:
- Remove Swagger annotations from route files.
- Update container data fetching to include CPU usage as a percentage.
- Improve error handling in container data fetching.
- Refactor frontend configuration controllers for better error handling.
- Update high availability controllers for improved error handling and file management.
- Improve logging and error handling in configuration handlers.
- Update notification template handling to improve error handling and data parsing.
- Refactor Docker client retrieval and add debug logging.
- Update logger to filter exit listener logs and improve formatting.

author: barneygale
body:
Add the following private methods to `pathlib.Path.info`:

- `_posix_permissions()`: the POSIX file permissions (`S_IMODE(st_mode)`)
- `_file_id()`: the file ID (`(st_dev, st_ino)`)
- `_access_time_ns()`: the access time in nanoseconds (`st_atime_ns`)
- `_mod_time_ns()`: the modify time in nanoseconds (`st_mtime_ns`)
- `_bsd_flags()`: the BSD file flags (`st_flags`)
- `_xattrs()`: the file extended attributes as a list of key, value pairs, or an empty list if `listxattr()` or `getxattr()` fail in an ignorable way.

These methods replace `LocalCopyReader.read_metadata()`, and so we can delete the `CopyReader` and `LocalCopyReader` classes. Rather than reading metadata via `source._copy_reader.read_metadata()`, we instead call `source.info._posix_permissions()`, `_access_time_ns()`, etc.

Preserving metadata is only supported for local-to-local copies at the moment. To support copying metadata between arbitrary `ReadablePath` and `WritablePath` objects, we'd need to make the new methods public and documented.

- Adds a dropdown for favorite issue labels directly on the board.

- Adds a `favorite_issue_labels` to visualizations, which can be updated via the VisualizationsController#update action
- Creates a reusable favorite_issue_labels_controller.js within the visualizations namespace.
- The stimulus controller is inside the visualizations namespace
- Although the feature could be reused on the the 'All Issues' view, implementing it there would require a 'favorite labels' field at the project level. In addition, this view in the future can have bulk editing (PRO Edition), making it less relevant to apply labels via shortcut (and also avoids future UI logic complications).

author: eepson123tw
body:
# Description

This PR significantly refines the Vortex component, enhancing performance, readability, and maintainability.  The core improvements focus on optimizing particle data management and the rendering pipeline.

Here's a summary of the key changes:

1.  **`Float32Array` for Particle Data:** All particle properties (position, velocity, life, etc.) are now stored in a single `Float32Array`. This drastically reduces memory overhead and improves access speed compared to using individual JavaScript objects for each particle.

2.  **`shallowRef` for Efficient Updates:** The `particleProps` are managed with `shallowRef`. This ensures that Vue only reacts to changes in the array's *reference*, not its internal contents. Since we directly mutate the `Float32Array`, this is crucial for preventing unnecessary component re-renders.

3.  **Particle Caching:** A `particleCache` object is introduced to minimize redundant calculations and array accesses within the animation loop.  Particle properties are loaded into the cache, calculations are performed, and then the `Float32Array` is updated once per particle.

4.  **Consolidated Rendering:** The rendering logic is streamlined into a single `draw` function, directly manipulating the canvas context. This eliminates redundant function calls and improves clarity.

5.  **Debounced Resize Handling:**  `useDebounceFn` is used to debounce window resize events.  This prevents excessive canvas re-renders during rapid resizing, leading to a smoother user experience.

6. **Code cleanup:** Improved variable and function name more descriptive, use uppercase for constant variables.

7. **Type improvements:** Improved some type definition.

**Overall Impact:**

These changes result in a significantly more performant and maintainable Vortex component. The use of `Float32Array` and `shallowRef` are key to the performance improvements, while the simplified rendering and debounced resizing enhance the user experience. The code is now cleaner, more readable, and follows best practices for Vue 3 and canvas animation.
